assertion.name: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mouse (conduction and fibrosis phenotype)
assertion.genotype: Cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout via alpha-MHC (Myh6)-Cre (Prdm16-null hearts); the driver is not named in this paper's own abstract-only record here and is attributed by PMID:37395136, which identifies its model as similar to Nam et al's Myh6-Cre knockout
assertion.description: Cardiac-restricted Prdm16 null model phenotyped by electrocardiography, fibrosis histology and left ventricular RNA sequencing. It is the only model in this entry that measures TGF-beta pathway activity in vivo and then tests it pharmacologically: TGF-beta signaling is activated in Prdm16-null hearts, but blocking the TGF-beta receptor does not rescue the conduction defect. That negative rescue result separates the fibrotic and conduction arms of the mechanism, and the accompanying ion-channel transcript dysregulation offers a TGF-beta-independent route to the arrhythmia node.

modeled_mechanisms.description: TGF-beta signaling is activated in Prdm16-null hearts at both ligand transcript and downstream effector level, the direction predicted by PRDM16 acting as a repressor of TGFB transcription.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: This model's direction conflicts with the Prdm16Q187X heterozygote, which shows age-dependent loss of TGF-beta expression. The two differ in allele class (complete cardiac null versus a heterozygous nonsense variant), dose and timepoint. The Q187X paper proposes that PRDM16 regulates TGF-beta bidirectionally in a temporally-dependent manner, which would make the two findings phases of one mechanism; that has not been tested across models, so the sign of the TGF-beta change in human LVNC8 should not be inferred from either model alone. The driver is alpha-MHC (Myh6)-Cre, attributed by PMID:37395136 rather than stated in this paper's own record here, and it matters: Myh6-Cre knockouts are reported to give hypertrophy in one model and LV dilation in another, and a later paper judged the earlier conditional Prdm16 lines not to mirror the patient LVNC phenotype.

readouts.name: Myocardial TGF-beta ligand transcripts and Smad2 phosphorylation
readouts.description: Quantitative real-time PCR for Tgfb1-3 and immunoblot for phosphorylated Smad2 in Prdm16-null hearts.
readouts.interpretation: Raised ligand transcripts together with increased phospho-Smad2 is pathway activation measured at two levels rather than a transcript change alone.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Prdm16-null hearts develop increased fibrosis with cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, quantified by trichrome staining, densitometry and hydroxyproline assay and accompanied by upregulated extracellular-matrix and myofibroblast transcripts.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Fibrosis here is measured in a complete cardiac null; patients are heterozygous, and no quantitative human myocardial fibrosis data exist for PRDM16 carriers to calibrate the magnitude against.

readouts.name: Myocardial collagen content
readouts.description: Trichrome staining with densitometry and hydroxyproline assay in Prdm16-null hearts versus wild-type.
readouts.interpretation: Three independent measures of collagen burden agreeing in direction is what makes this more than a histological impression.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Prdm16-null hearts show measurable conduction and repolarization abnormalities (prolonged QRS and QTc) alongside dysregulated ion channel transcripts, giving a TGF-beta-independent substrate for the arrhythmia node.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The phenotype is conduction slowing and repolarization prolongation, not the accessory-pathway pre-excitation that names this node; no pre-excitation is reported in this model. Blocking the TGF-beta receptor does not reverse the conduction abnormality, so the arrhythmic substrate here is not downstream of the TGF-beta arm and should not be treated as such.

readouts.interpretation: Prolonged QRS and QTc are the quantitative conduction and repolarization abnormalities behind this node in this model.

readouts.description: RNA sequencing of left ventricular tissue, assessed for ion channel gene expression.
readouts.interpretation: Dysregulation of Kcne1, Scn5a, Cacna1h and Cacna2d2 is the proposed molecular basis of the conduction phenotype and is independent of the TGF-beta arm.

selected_evidence.snippet: We used cardiac-specific Prdm16 conditional knockout mice to examine cardiac function by electrocardiography.

value.name: Prdm16 cardiomyocyte-specific knockout mouse (Prdm16cKO)
value.genotype: Prdm16 conditional knockout, cardiomyocyte-restricted via Xmlc2-Cre and, independently, cTnT-Cre (both lines called Prdm16cKO in the paper)
value.description: Conditional deletion of Prdm16 restricted to cardiomyocytes. Unlike earlier conditional Prdm16 lines, this model reproduces the left-ventricle-selective vulnerability seen in patients: it develops LV-specific dilation and systolic dysfunction together with biventricular noncompaction. Paired RNA sequencing, ChIP sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics in the same model identify the direct transcriptional targets of PRDM16 and show that compact-layer cardiomyocytes lose their normal transcriptomic identity. It is the reference in vivo model for the compact-myocardium transcriptional arm of the LVNC8 mechanism.

assertion.description: The model develops biventricular noncompaction, the structural lesion this node names.
assertion.limitations: Noncompaction here is biventricular, whereas the human disease label and the patient phenotype foreground the left ventricle; the chamber distribution is therefore broader in the model than in patients.

selected_evidence.snippet: Cardiomyocyte-specific ablation of Prdm16 in mice caused LV-specific dilation and dysfunction, as well as biventricular noncompaction, which fully recapitulated LVNC in patients.

assertion.name: Prdm16 cardiomyocyte-specific deletion mouse (conduction-system phenotype)
assertion.genotype: Prdm16lox/lox;Sm22alpha-Cre (called Prdm16cKO in the paper), deleting Prdm16 exon 9 in cardiomyocytes from early cardiac development onward
assertion.description: An independently generated cardiomyocyte-specific Prdm16 deletion, analysed by combined single-cell RNA and ATAC sequencing. It is kept separate from the Prdm16cKO model above because it interrogates a different arm of the mechanism: rather than the compact-versus-trabecular axis, it establishes that PRDM16 suppresses conduction-system and atrial fates, and that its loss expands the distal ventricular conduction system. This is the only in vivo source for the conduction and arrhythmia arm of this entry.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Ventricular Conduction System Hyperplasia and Atrial-Fate Derepression
modeled_mechanisms.description: Developmental myocardial Prdm16 loss expands the distal ventricular conduction system, the structural change this node asserts.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The Sm22alpha-Cre driver is not cardiomyocyte-exclusive: the authors report that it also eliminates PRDM16 in smooth muscle cells, and argue the cardiomyocyte loss is the primary culprit on the grounds that smooth muscle coverage was unaffected. Deletion is also developmental, where patients carry partial lifelong haploinsufficiency; whether that produces conduction-system expansion of comparable extent has not been shown, and no human histological counterpart is available.

assertion.name: Hypoglycin A and MCPA immersion in zebrafish embryos and larvae
assertion.description: Wild-type AB embryos were exposed by immersion beginning at 24 hours after fertilization, with monitoring through 96 hours. HGA and MCPA produced mortality, bradycardia and cardiac edema, with later toxicity onset after HGA; MCPA also reduced swimming under selected exposure conditions. The model was developed for Sapindaceae-associated equine atypical myopathy and captures shared toxin biology rather than human ackee ingestion or a demonstrated human hypoglycemic syndrome. Whole-body metabolite and locomotor experiments each had one experimental replicate; metabolomics pooled twenty larvae per concentration. Mortality assays used biological triplicates. Glycine and carnitine co-exposure reduced 72-hour mortality, whereas riboflavin did not protect in this protocol. Compounds were added simultaneously with toxin, so this is prevention/co-treatment evidence, not treatment after established poisoning. Surviving larvae could retain cardiac abnormalities. MCPrG caused no observed toxicity in this exposure system, but uptake and activation were unresolved; the result does not establish safety in mammals.

modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Indirect bioactivation readout from pooled whole-body material with no biological replicate series; neither MCPA-CoA nor a specific activating enzyme was directly quantified. Immersion differs from oral human exposure.

assertion.description: Cx47-null mice are fertile and show no obvious morphological or behavioural abnormality. The single knockout does not produce the human motor disease.

modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Two limits bound what this model shows. And the design intent was only partly met: the knock-in was made so a truncated mutant protein could be tested for toxic gain-of-function, but TECPR2 was undetectable at the protein level, so functionally this remains a loss-of-expression model like the knockout.

modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Two limits bound what this model shows. assertion.name: Mybpc3-targeted knock-in mouse (homozygous exon 6 G>A)
assertion.genotype: Mybpc3 knock-in, homozygous G>A transition in exon 6
assertion.description: A homozygous Mybpc3 knock-in mouse carrying a single point mutation that generates three aberrant mRNAs, developed as a hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy model but genotypically in the biallelic regime this entry curates. modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The rescued phenotype is hypertrophy with cardiac dysfunction, not noncompaction, so the experiment shows that a biallelic Mybpc3 cardiac phenotype is correctable rather than that the human LVNC10 compaction defect specifically is. The authors also report the effect as transient and requiring optimization, and the construct is exon-6-specific, so it would not transfer to the human truncating alleles curated in this entry without redesign.

divergences.description: The corrected lesion is a mouse exon-6 splice-shifting point mutation. The human LVNC10 alleles are frameshift and nonsense variants distributed across the gene, for which this exon-skipping strategy offers no direct route.
The rescue is reported as transient, so the experiment bounds a short-term prevention window and says nothing about durable correction of the organ-level failure node.

assertion.name: mybpc3 knockout zebrafish
assertion.genotype: mybpc3 stable knockout (heterozygous and homozygous)
assertion.description:
A stable zebrafish knockout of the cMyBP-C orthologue, built as a hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy model but carrying the finding that matters most to this entry: immunofluorescence shows significant cardiomyocyte hyperplasia in mutant hearts at the larval stage (608 vs 302 total cardiomyocyte nuclei), with myocardial remodeling and hyperplasia persisting into later larval development. That is the same cellular response the homozygous cMyBP-C-deficient mouse shows, reached independently in a teleost, which is the strongest support this entry carries for treating hyperplasia as a conserved consequence of cMyBP-C loss rather than a murine idiosyncrasy.
The direction of the wall phenotype is the point to keep hold of. Zebrafish do form a compact ventricular myocardium over a trabecular layer, and this knockout does not fail to compact it - the mutant ventricle and atrium became *more* compact, with a thicker myocardial wall and smaller chamber diameters. So the one model here that could in principle have shown a compaction defect showed the opposite.

modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The zebrafish heart is two-chambered and the gene is an orthologue rather than human MYBPC3, so the model speaks to conserved cMyBP-C cell biology and not to human ventricular architecture. value.name: Homozygous cMyBP-C-deficient mouse (Mybpc3 t/t)
value.genotype: Mybpc3 t/t (homozygous cardiac myosin binding protein C-deficient)
value.description: The homozygous cMyBP-C-deficient mouse is the murine counterpart of the biallelic MYBPC3 allelic state that defines LVNC10, and is the only model in this entry that offers a candidate mechanism for the dose-phenotype divergence recorded in the open discussion below. These mice enlarge their hearts almost twofold shortly after birth, and the enlargement is driven by myocyte hyperplasia rather than hypertrophy: cMyBP-C-null myocytes complete an extra round of postnatal cell division and accumulate as supernumerary mononuclear cells, whereas the heterozygous state produces hypertrophy through increased cell size. The authors propose that cMyBP-C normally acts as an inhibitor of postnatal myocyte cytokinesis, so that near-complete loss releases a proliferative program at exactly the window in which the mammalian ventricle is finishing its trabecular-to-compact remodeling.

assertion.description: The model reproduces the allelic dose and the neonatal timing of the human compaction phenotype, and supplies a cellular mechanism - failure of postnatal myocyte cell-cycle exit - that could plausibly divert ventricular wall maturation. It does not reproduce the noncompaction phenotype itself.
assertion.limitations: The mouse phenotype is cardiac dilation with myocyte hyperplasia, not a persistently hypertrabeculated, noncompacted ventricular wall; the abstract reports no trabecular-to-compact remodeling measurement. Homozygous null mice also survive into adulthood, where the human biallelic genotype is lethal within months. Treating the cytokinesis finding as the explanation of human compaction failure is an inference the cited work does not make.

divergences.description: The measured quantity is the number of postnatal myocyte divisions and the resulting count of mononuclear myocytes. The node's quantity is the extent of trabecular-to-compact remodeling of the ventricular wall. Extra cell divisions are a candidate upstream cause of a compaction defect, not a measurement of one.

The model observes cell-cycle behaviour in individual cardiomyocytes (CELLULAR); the node is the tissue-level architecture of the ventricular wall (TISSUE). The step from supernumerary myocytes to a noncompacted wall is not observed in this model.

Murine and human ventricular compaction differ in timing relative to birth, and the mouse null survives to adulthood while the equivalent human genotype is fatal in the first months of life, so the postnatal-proliferation window the model exploits may not be the window in which the human phenotype is set.

readouts.interpretation: The cellular readout standing in for the compaction node: extended postnatal proliferation is the model's proposed route from cMyBP-C loss to abnormal ventricular wall maturation.

selected_evidence.snippet: However, the mechanism leading to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in heterozygous MYBPC3(+/-) individuals is myocyte hypertrophy (increased cell size), whereas the mechanism leading to cardiac dilation in homozygous Mybpc3(-/-) mice is primarily myocyte hyperplasia.

value.name: Constitutive and Adult-Inducible Mir96 Knockout Mice
value.genotype: Mir96 null or UBC CreERT2/+; Mir96 fl/fl
value.description: Single-gene loss-of-function comparators. Constitutive heterozygotes retained normal hearing through three months, whereas homozygotes progressively lost hearing. Adult biallelic inducible deletion caused hearing loss four weeks after tamoxifen at five months, without detectable cell loss at that time. HC-specific, but not SGN-specific, conditional deletion reproduced the early hearing defect. Neonatal AAV8-miR-96 delivery partially rescued null mice; sustained benefit remained in only a subset, and this was not a test of rescue of a dominant seed variant.

assertion.description: Adult deletion tests the maintenance requirement separately from congenital maturation effects.
assertion.limitations: Deletion lacks a mutant target repertoire; the adult inducible driver is systemic, and transcriptomes use mixed whole-cochlear tissue. These experiments do not model dominant human alleles.

readouts.name: ABR thresholds after adult Mir96 deletion
readouts.interpretation: Hearing thresholds rise after adult depletion, before detectable hair-cell or SGN loss.

selected_evidence.snippet: the restorative effects were maintained in 50% and 38% of AAV8-miR-96-treated miR-96−/− mice at 2 and 3 months of age, respectively

value.name: Mir96 +14C>A human-allele knock-in mouse
value.genotype: Mir96 tm3.1Wtsi (Mir96 +14C>A knock-in), heterozygous and homozygous
value.description: Knock-in of the human +14C>A allele from Spanish family s1334. Heterozygotes develop progressive high-frequency-first hearing loss and bundle abnormalities; homozygotes are profoundly impaired. This line supports editing and pharmacological proof-of-concept studies, with species and C57BL/6N background limitations.

assertion.description: Two independent preclinical rescue arms have been run in this line. AAV delivery of SaCas9-KKH with a guide RNA against the mutant allele into the cochleae of presymptomatic and symptomatic adult mice improved hearing long term, with better results from earlier injection. Separately, amitriptyline - selected by matching the mutant transcriptome against anti-correlated drug expression profiles - delayed progression at high frequencies.
assertion.limitations: Both interventions remain preclinical. Editing disrupts the mutant allele, preserves surviving cells and is ineffective when delivered at sixteen weeks. Low standard-dose vector integration and assay-limited off-target results do not establish human safety. Amitriptyline exposure began with breeding parents and continued in offspring, delayed progression only temporarily, did not improve homozygotes and showed no additional benefit at double dose; the authors did not recommend it for human treatment.

readouts.name: Hearing preservation after adult cochlear AAV-SaCas9-KKH editing
readouts.interpretation: ABR and DPOAE thresholds were lower than untreated contralateral ears after early treatment, representing partial hearing preservation rather than normalization.

readouts.name: High-frequency threshold progression under oral amitriptyline
readouts.interpretation: Progression is delayed rather than halted or reversed, which is why the direction is ALTERED and not RESTORED.

selected_evidence.snippet: This is a proof of concept rather than a suggestion that amitriptyline be used as a treatment for humans carrying the MIR96+14C>A mutation, for several reasons.

value.name: Mir183/96 double-knockout mouse
value.genotype: Mir183/96 null (Mir183 and Mir96 deleted together), heterozygous and homozygous
value.description: Deletion of Mir183 and Mir96 provides a loss-of-function comparator. Heterozygous hearing thresholds resemble wild type through six months; homozygotes have profound hearing loss, bundle abnormalities and reduced IHC synapses. Comparing this model with seed mutants supports an acquired-target contribution, with co-deletion, strain and expression-platform confounding.

assertion.target: Repression of Novel Targets Acquired by the Mutant Seed
assertion.description: The deleted allele cannot produce a mutant seed RNA. Normal heterozygous hearing argues against simple dosage insufficiency in this model but does not resolve the mechanism of every human precursor allele.
assertion.limitations: The deletion removes Mir183 as well as Mir96, so a comparison against a seed mutant confounds the two microRNAs; and the transcriptomes were compared across studies rather than in one experiment. The conclusion is an inference from a phenotype and transcriptome contrast, not a direct demonstration that any particular acquired target drives the disease.

readouts.name: Hearing in null heterozygotes
readouts.target: Repression of Novel Targets Acquired by the Mutant Seed
readouts.interpretation: Normal heterozygous thresholds support a mechanism beyond reduced dosage for dominant seed alleles; they do not prove that partial loss of normal targeting is irrelevant.

selected_evidence.snippet: We propose three mechanisms of action of mutant miRNAs; loss of targets that are normally completely repressed, loss of targets whose transcription is normally buffered by the miRNA, and gain of novel targets.

value.name: diminuendo (Mir96 Dmdo) ENU seed-mutant mouse
value.genotype: Mir96 Dmdo (ENU-induced single-base substitution in the miR-96 seed region), heterozygous and homozygous
value.description: ENU-derived Mir96 +15A>T seed mutant, distinct from the human alleles. Heterozygotes develop severe early auditory impairment and later hair-cell loss; homozygotes have profound impairment and complete neonatal maturation arrest. Transcriptomic motif enrichment supports both lost normal targeting and acquired targeting, subsequently also demonstrated in the human-seed knock-in models.

assertion.description: Single-cell physiology establishes neonatal maturation arrest in homozygotes, with an intermediate heterozygous phenotype. This is one component of miR-96 biology rather than proof of an exclusively developmental human disorder.
assertion.limitations: Complete maturation arrest was characterized in neonatal homozygous mice; heterozygotes show intermediate changes. The reported human families carry heterozygous alleles and develop postlingual hearing loss, so neonatal mouse timing is not established human natural history.

readouts.name: Biophysical differentiation of inner versus outer hair cells
readouts.interpretation: Homozygous mutant cells retain immature biophysical properties; heterozygotes have intermediate defects.

readouts.name: Auditory brainstem or compound action potential threshold
readouts.interpretation: Thresholds rise by about 60 dB in heterozygotes - a higher threshold means worse hearing - and no response is obtainable in homozygotes.

selected_evidence.snippet: Moreover, maturation of the hair cell stereocilia bundle and remodelling of auditory nerve connections within the cochlea fail to occur in miR-96 mutants.

assertion.name: Thra1PV/+ dominant-negative TR-alpha1 mouse
assertion.genotype: Thra1PV/+ (frameshift TRalpha1PV mutant, heterozygous)
assertion.description: A knock-in mouse expressing a frameshift TR-alpha1 mutant that shares its mutated C-terminal sequence with human THRA frameshift variants. Crossing it with the Ncor1-delta-ID mouse, whose NCOR1 cannot be recruited by the mutant receptor, partially reverses growth retardation, delayed bone development and infertility - which makes this the experiment that established corepressor recruitment as the operative mechanism in vivo rather than an in vitro inference.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Persistent Corepressor Occupancy at Thyroid Hormone Response Elements
modeled_mechanisms.description: The defining test: removing the mutant receptor's ability to recruit NCOR1 relieves the phenotype, so the phenotype is a consequence of corepressor recruitment.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The rescue arm uses a genetically engineered NCOR1 that cannot be recruited, not a pharmacological intervention, so it establishes mechanism without demonstrating a tractable human target. The rescue is also explicitly partial.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reproduces growth retardation and delayed bone development, both partially reversible by blocking NCOR1 recruitment.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The mouse additionally shows infertility, which is not a reported feature of human RTH-alpha, so the phenotype is not a clean match; and the human skeletal picture includes epiphyseal dysgenesis and delayed dentition that the cited work does not assess.

modeled_mechanisms.description: TR-alpha1PV directly suppresses key erythroid genes and impairs erythroid progenitor differentiation and terminal erythropoiesis; blocking NCOR1 recruitment corrects both. The corresponding human feature - anaemia in about 77% of reported cases - is one of the commonest findings.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The mouse rescue corrects erythroid differentiation, whereas human anaemia largely persists on levothyroxine. That is not a contradiction - the interventions differ - but it means the model's reversibility should not be read as predicting treatment response.

selected_evidence.snippet: TRα1PV shares the same C-terminal mutated sequences as those of patients with frameshift mutations of the THRA gene.

value.name: thraa / thrab CRISPR dominant-negative zebrafish
value.genotype: thrab 1-bp insertion and thraa 8-bp insertion dominant-negative alleles
value.description: Germline-transmissible CRISPR/Cas9 dominant-negative alleles in the two duplicated zebrafish thra genes. Homozygous thrab mutants show severe growth retardation with markedly suppressed growth hormone and IGF1 expression, while homozygous thraa mutants are only mildly affected. The same species is the model in which the corepressor-dissociating ligand analogue ES08 rescued developmental anomalies.

assertion.description: Reproduces severe postlarval growth retardation and identifies suppressed gh1 and igf1 expression as a proximate cause.
assertion.limitations: Zebrafish have two thra paralogues where humans have one, and the phenotype partitions unequally between them, so the genotype is not comparable to a human heterozygote. The informative alleles are homozygous, whereas human RTH-alpha is heterozygous and dominant-negative. Zebrafish also have no growth plate, so endochondral ossification - the mechanism this node names - is not what is being observed.

divergences.description: The thra locus is duplicated in zebrafish into thraa and thrab, and the growth phenotype is carried almost entirely by thrab. There is no single ortholog whose disruption corresponds to a human THRA heterozygote, so allele dosage and gene identity both diverge.
The measured quantity is body growth with gh1 and igf1 transcript levels. The node's quantity is growth plate chondrocyte maturation and endochondral ossification, which zebrafish do not have.

selected_evidence.snippet: Expression of the growth hormone (gh1) and insulin-like growth factor 1 was markedly suppressed in homozygous thrab 1-bp ins (m/m) mutants.

assertion.name: TR-alpha1 mutant cardiac telemetry mouse
assertion.genotype: TRalpha1 mutant (male)
assertion.description: Cardiac telemetry in male TR-alpha1 mutant mice localized the bradycardia of RTH-alpha to the heart itself rather than to autonomic outflow, and transcriptomics showed preserved T3-dependent upregulation of the pacemaker channels Hcn2 and Hcn4 alongside irreversibly reduced expression of other heart-rate ion channel genes. Raising maternal T3 in utero restored that expression and the DNA methylation of Ryr2, implying a developmental window.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Reproduces the persistent bradycardia and demonstrates it is intrinsic to the heart, matching the clinical observation that thyroxine does not raise heart rate in patients.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Only male mice were studied. The in utero maternal T3 rescue has no human counterpart - RTH-alpha is not diagnosed prenatally, precisely because there is no screening signal - so the developmental-window finding is not currently actionable.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mutations in thyroid hormone receptor α1 (TRα1) cause Resistance to Thyroid Hormone α (RTHα), a disorder characterized by hypothyroidism in TRα1-expressing tissues including the heart.

assertion.name: Low-T3-affinity TR-alpha1 knock-in mouse (TH rescue model)
assertion.genotype: TRalpha1 knock-in with 10-fold reduced thyroid hormone affinity, heterozygous
assertion.description: A heterozygous knock-in mouse whose TR-alpha1 binds thyroid hormone with 10-fold lower affinity, producing extreme anxiety, reduced recognition memory and locomotor dysfunction. Its value here is the rescue design rather than the phenotype: it separates the CNS consequences into two classes with different therapeutic windows. Anxiety and memory deficits were relieved by high-dose thyroid hormone given in adulthood, correlating with normalized GABAergic inhibitory interneurons in hippocampal CA1, whereas the locomotor dysfunction required post-natal treatment and was linked to otherwise delayed cerebellar development.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Impaired Central Nervous System Thyroid Hormone Action
modeled_mechanisms.description: Thyroid hormone rescues part of the CNS phenotype, and the part it rescues depends on when it is given. This is the closest experimental evidence bearing on whether levothyroxine started late can help, which is the open clinical question for this disorder.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The lesion is reduced ligand affinity, not the dominant-negative corepressor retention that causes human RTH-alpha, so a hormone-dose rescue is expected to work better here than in a patient whose mutant receptor is transcriptionally inert. The rescued readouts are rodent behavioural assays (anxiety, recognition memory, locomotion), which map only loosely onto the human phenotype of dyspraxia, dysarthria and reduced IQ. Treatment was high-dose thyroid hormone in a mouse, not a clinical levothyroxine regimen.

divergences.description: The measured quantities are murine anxiety, recognition memory and locomotor performance. The node's quantity is impaired thyroid hormone action in the human central nervous system, manifesting as developmental delay, dyspraxia and intellectual disability.

selected_evidence.snippet: we introduced a mutation into the mouse TRalpha1 gene that lowers affinity to thyroid hormone (TH) 10-fold

assertion.name: Slc17a8 null mouse
assertion.genotype: Slc17a8 (Vglut3) exon 2 targeted deletion, homozygous null
assertion.description: Homozygous Slc17a8 null mice model complete loss of vesicular glutamate transmission with profound hearing loss and extra-cochlear effects including seizures. The published vestibular study found strongly reduced quantal transmission but relatively preserved spontaneous vestibular nerve activity and most balance tests, with some assay differences. Nonquantal compensation is proposed; this is not proof of normal human vestibular function.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Impaired Glutamate Release at the Inner Hair Cell Ribbon Synapse
modeled_mechanisms.description: The release failure and its localisation to vesicle content rather than fusion, both measured directly in the correct cell type.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Homozygous null mice model complete VGLUT3 loss, not the heterozygous human genotypes. Congenital profound deafness and mouse epilepsy do not reproduce the typical progressive nonsyndromic presentation.

readouts.name: Calcium-triggered synaptic vesicle turnover in inner hair cells
readouts.target: Impaired Glutamate Release at the Inner Hair Cell Ribbon Synapse
readouts.interpretation: Exocytosis itself is normal. A deliberate negative result, and the one that makes the defect a cargo defect rather than a release-machinery defect.

readouts.name: Ribbon synapse ultrastructure at three months
readouts.target: Impaired Glutamate Release at the Inner Hair Cell Ribbon Synapse
readouts.interpretation: Surviving ribbons appeared normal in this line at three months despite reduced synapse numbers. Other null-model studies reported altered ribbon shape; this result is specific to this study.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Failure of Auditory Nerve Activation with Preserved Cochlear Amplification
modeled_mechanisms.description: The three-way dissociation - no acoustic neural response, intact emissions, intact electrically evoked brainstem response - measured in one animal.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Detailed human OAE/ABR testing in the 2003 report concerns one proband. The mouse dissociation cannot establish the physiology of all carriers or clinical implant outcomes.

readouts.name: Otoacoustic emissions
readouts.target: Failure of Auditory Nerve Activation with Preserved Cochlear Amplification
readouts.interpretation: Outer hair cell amplification is preserved, placing the lesion downstream of the cochlear amplifier. A negative result, and the load-bearing one.

readouts.name: Electrically evoked auditory brainstem response
readouts.target: Failure of Auditory Nerve Activation with Preserved Cochlear Amplification
readouts.interpretation: The ascending auditory pathway can still be driven when the defective synapse is bypassed, which is the observation that makes cochlear implantation biologically plausible in this disease.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Secondary Deafferentation of the Inner Hair Cell
modeled_mechanisms.description: The afferent synapses, spiral ganglion neurons and lateral efferent endings decline after the functional deficit is established.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The null model has complete congenital loss of signaling and developmental neuronal effects. Human onset is variable and usually later; human synapse-count evidence is lacking in the reviewed sources.

readouts.name: Afferent synapse and spiral ganglion neuron counts
readouts.target: Secondary Deafferentation of the Inner Hair Cell
readouts.interpretation: The afferent population beneath the inner hair cell falls over time in the null animal.

selected_evidence.snippet: We propose that non-quantal transmission is sufficient to support vestibular nerve physiology and behavioral function in Vglut3 −/− mice.

value.name: VGLUT3 A224V knock-in mouse
value.genotype: Slc17a8 p.A224V knock-in (mouse equivalent of human p.A211V), homozygous
value.description: The allele-matched model, and the reason this entry carries two hypothesis groups. A single point mutation was introduced into exon 5 of mouse Slc17a8, exchanging the codon for the alanine that corresponds to human A211. It reproduces the progressive course the null mouse does not, and it reaches a different conclusion about where the disease starts.

assertion.target: Inner Hair Cell Stereocilia Bundle Disruption
assertion.description: Collapse and fusion of the inner hair cell stereocilia bundles, with outer hair cell bundles spared - the model's primary structural finding.
assertion.limitations: Homozygosity differs from human dominant inheritance. The C57BL/6J Cdh23 background may modify the bundle phenotype; this has not been separated experimentally. No corresponding human cochlear morphology was demonstrated.

readouts.name: Inner hair cell stereocilia bundle morphology by scanning electron microscopy
readouts.target: Inner Hair Cell Stereocilia Bundle Disruption
readouts.interpretation: Inner hair cell bundles collapse; outer hair cell bundles do not. The contrast within the same cochlea is what makes this a cell-type-specific lesion rather than general degeneration.

selected_evidence.snippet: These results suggest that DFNA25 stems from a failure in the mechano-transduction followed by a change in synaptic transfer.
